derivations.claim: In a local unitary frame let $F_{\det A}$ be the curvature of the induced connection on $\det E$. The induced connection on the top exterior power has local connection matrix $\operatorname{tr}A$, hence $F_{\det A}=\operatorname{tr}F_A$. Put $\eta=-i\operatorname{tr}F_A$, a real two-form because $F_A$ is anti-Hermitian. By [F2], $d\eta=0$, and the linearity of trace in $F_A^+=0$ gives $*_g\eta=-\eta$.

Choose the unit vector $v_\infty$ in $(\det E)_\infty$ specified by the determinant of the framing. For any $x\in S^4$, parallel transport $v_\infty$ along a piecewise smooth path from $\infty$ to $x$. If two paths are chosen, their concatenation is a loop. By [F3] the loop is null-homotopic; subdivide a null-homotopy square into finitely many rectangles mapped into coordinate balls, which is possible by compactness and a Lebesgue number for the pulled-back coordinate-ball cover. On each rectangle [F4] makes boundary transport the identity. Multiplying around the subdivision cancels the interior edges, so the two path transports agree. The resulting section is smooth by local parallel frames, is parallel by construction, and agrees with $v_\infty$; uniqueness follows from uniqueness of parallel sections along each path. Its unit norm is preserved by unitary parallel transport, so the determinant framing reduces the structure group to $SU(N)$.

By [A1] and [F3], $\eta$ is exact, so choose a smooth real one-form $\alpha$ with $\eta=d\alpha$. The ASD equation gives $\int_{S^4}\eta\wedge *_g\eta=-\int_{S^4}d\alpha\wedge\eta=-\int_{S^4}d(\alpha\wedge\eta)=0$, since $d\eta=0$ and $S^4$ is compact without boundary. The integrand $\eta\wedge *_g\eta$ is the nonnegative squared norm density of the real form $\eta$; zero integral forces $\eta=0$ pointwise. Hence $F_{\det A}=0$ and the determinant connection is flat.

Writing $C=-F_A/(2\pi i)$, the degree-four term of $\det(I+C)$ is $c_2(A)=\tfrac12((\operatorname{tr}C)\wedge(\operatorname{tr}C)-\operatorname{tr}(C\wedge C))$. Step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so this reduces to $c_2(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$. Therefore $q_N=-\int_{S^4}c_2(A)$. By [F5] and the de Rham integration pairing, $\int_{S^4}c_2(A)=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$, an integer. Finally $q_N=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int B(F_A\wedge F_A)$ for the positive invariant form $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$; since $F_A=-*_gF_A$ and $B$ is positive definite, $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int B(F_A\wedge *_gF_A)\leq0$. This proves the stated sign and nonnegativity of $k=-q_N$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the universal line family is a proper flat projective family and $e^*\mathcal E$ is coherent and flat over $G$. By [F2], every real fibre has $H^0$ of dimension $N$ and vanishing $H^1$. The stated surjectivity and [F3] with $q=0$ make $p_*e^*\mathcal E$ locally free of rank $N$ near each real-line point, and identify its fibre with $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$. Restriction to the smooth real locus $S^4\subset G$ therefore gives a smooth rank-$N$ bundle.

The evaluation morphism $p^*p_*e^*\mathcal E\to e^*\mathcal E$ restricts over each real line to the evaluation map $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})\otimes\mathcal O_{L_x}\to\mathcal E|_{L_x}$. The unitary holomorphic trivialization in the Statement makes this a fibrewise isomorphism at every point of $L_x$.

Fix a parameter $[L_x]$ satisfying the surjectivity hypothesis. By [F3], after shrinking a complex-open neighbourhood $U\subseteq G$, the sheaf $p_*e^*\mathcal E$ is locally free there and all degree-zero base-change maps are isomorphisms. Thus evaluation is a map between rank-$N$ vector bundles on $p^{-1}(U)$. Its non-isomorphism locus is closed, as it is the zero locus of its determinant. The morphism $p$ is proper, so the image of this closed set is closed in $U$. Step 2.1 shows that this image does not contain $[L_x]$; shrinking $U$ again makes it empty. Hence evaluation is an isomorphism on every line in this smaller neighbourhood. Restriction to the real locus gives the asserted incidence isomorphism, smooth variation of the Hermitian forms, and the induced framing at infinity.

derivations.claim: For a framed ASD connection $A$, pull $E$ back to $Z$. Define $\bar\partial_{\mathcal E}$ by the ordinary Dolbeault operator along each vertical twistor line and by $A^{0,1}$ on horizontal vectors. The vertical square is zero. A mixed vertical-horizontal commutator is zero because the vertical connection is constant on the fibre $E_x$ and vertical vectors project to zero on $S^4$. On two horizontal $(0,1)$ vectors the square is $F_A$ evaluated on their projected plane $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. By [F1] and $F_A^+=0$, this restriction vanishes, so $\bar\partial_{\mathcal E}^2=0$.

Apply [A3] to obtain the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$. Its restriction to each real line is the constant holomorphic bundle with fibre $E_x$, so it is holomorphically and unitarily trivial. The Hermitian metric induces the positive Ward reality datum, and the framing at $\infty$ gives the framing on $L_\infty$. The first-order-extension connection recovers $A$ because extending a constant section differentiates it by the original covariant derivative; hence the induced Hermitian form is parallel. By [F4] and the twistor orientation, $q_N=-k$ gives $c_2(E)=ku$ and $c_2(\pi^*E)=kH^2$. Gauge-equivalent framed connections give isomorphic Ward bundles; [A1] supplies the stated algebraic comparison when an algebraic presentation is used.

For a Ward bundle, [A2] and [F3] make $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ a smooth rank-$N$ bundle and identify evaluation on every real line. The conormal bundle is $N^*_{L_x/Z}\cong\mathcal O(-1)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)$, so the first-neighbourhood sequence tensored by $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O^{\oplus N}$ is $0\to\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2N}\to\mathcal E|_{L_x^{(1)}}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus N}\to0$. By [F2], the left term has zero $H^0$ and $H^1$; its long exact sequence makes $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x^{(1)}})\to H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ an isomorphism. Every section therefore has a unique first-order holomorphic extension. Differentiating these extensions along the smooth family of lines gives a connection; the Leibniz rule follows by extending a product, and uniqueness makes the derivative depend only on the first jet. By [A4] this connection is unitary.

In the inverse Ward construction, the horizontal component of the square of the induced Dolbeault operator is $\widehat F$ on $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. It vanishes because the Ward bundle is holomorphic, so $\widehat F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B=0$ for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$. A homogeneous quadratic in two complex variables that vanishes at every projective point has all three coefficients zero; hence $\widehat F^+=0$ by [F1]. The unitary framing on $L_\infty$ and the evaluation isomorphism frame $\widehat E_\infty$.

Starting from $A$, constant sections identify $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ with $E_x$, and the first-order-extension connection is $A$ by step 1.2. Starting from a Ward bundle, [F3] identifies the reconstructed pullback bundle with $\mathcal E$ on every real line; evaluation is holomorphic vertically, and the horizontal Dolbeault derivatives agree by the first-order-extension definition, so evaluation is a holomorphic isomorphism on $Z$. Since $\pi^*u=H^2$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, naturality gives $\langle c_2(\widehat E),[S^4]\rangle=k$; [F4] then gives $q_N=-k$. The identifications preserve the Hermitian form and framing. No irreducibility is used, so flat summands pass through the same fibrewise section construction. Rotations and framing transformations commute with evaluation and extension, making the two maps inverse and $T$-equivariant on framed isomorphism classes.

Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be a real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all four coefficient bundles $F$.

Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty open subset of the line family of $P$; the incidence projection from this open subset covers a dense subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on every such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$, so it vanishes on a dense subset and is zero. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$.

Tensor $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ by $\mathcal E$. Step 1.2 gives $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=0$, and step 1.1 gives $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. The long exact sequence yields $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$. Serre duality and step 1.1 also give $H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring by $\mathcal E(-2)$ and twisting the output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal complex resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. Its only cohomology is the degree-zero hypercohomology of the diagonal resolution, namely $\mathcal E$; the first and last terms are exact because the other total degrees vanish. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Thus this is the stated monad; its cohomology vector spaces are canonical, and changing bases acts by $GL(U)\times GL(K)\times GL(U')$.

From [A3], $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E(t))=Ne^{tH}-kH^2e^{tH}$ and $\operatorname{td}(T_Z)=1+2H+\tfrac{11}{6}H^2+H^3$. Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch [F7] gives $\chi(\mathcal E(t))=N\binom{t+3}{3}-k(t+2)$, with values $k,-N+2k,0,-k$ for $t=-3,-4,-2,-1$. The Euler sequences $0\to\mathcal O(-4)\to\mathcal O(-3)^{\oplus4}\to\Omega_Z^2\to0$ and $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ give Euler characteristics $k,2k+N,k$ for the three monad coefficient bundles. Steps 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 leave only $H^2$ in each, so these values are the dimensions.

The space of parallel sections of $\widehat E$ evaluates to a trivial subbundle, and its orthogonal complement is parallel because the connection is unitary. No nonzero parallel section lies in the complement. Every flat summand is trivial since $S^4$ is simply connected [F2]. The Ward transform and diagonal construction preserve direct sums. For a trivial rank-$m$ summand $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}$, the two Euler sequences and [F6] give coefficient groups $H^2(\mathcal O(-3))=0$, $H^2(\Omega_Z^2)^{\oplus m}\cong\mathbb C^m$, and $H^2(\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$, so its monad is $0\to\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}\to0$. Flat summands are therefore included without imposing $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$ or $H^0(Z,\mathcal E^\vee)=0$. No Dirac index or kernel-dimension formula is used.

Thus retain [A1] as an independent obligation and do not infer the raw moment maps from Donaldson's displayed equations alone.

Assuming [A1], the normalized quaternionic change of basis produces a raw tuple satisfying both equations in [F2]. The pointwise full-rank equivalence in [A1] identifies its locus exactly with stable and costable data, so the tuple is regular. A unitary change of basis $g\in U(k)$ in the internal monad vector spaces acts on the tuple by $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$; conversely the uniqueness clause of [A1] says every normalized framed monad isomorphism has this form. Hence the normalized monad classes and raw regular $U(k)$ orbits agree conditionally on [A1].

By [A1], the orthogonal-kernel projection and its framing at infinity give the Ward connection and the inverse matrix extraction. Its ASD equation follows from the Ward correspondence [[thm-qftx-framed-penrose-ward-correspondence-on-s4]]. The monad Chern character and the oriented twistor pullback calculation in [F3], together with the framed determinant normalization [F4], give $k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N$. This completes the charge calculation once the exact block interface is established.

derivations.claim: By [A1], each regular zero-FI unitary orbit determines one regular complex $GL(k)$ orbit, and each regular complex orbit has exactly one balanced unitary representative. The two constructions are inverse because each orbit intersection is unique; the quotient map is a diffeomorphism in the word-frame charts. The exact torus action in [F1] commutes with both gauge actions, so this quotient identification is $T$-equivariant.

By [A2], every stable complex orbit gives one framed torsion-free $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf with the stated rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial, and the converse recovers the same orbit. Its locally-free locus is exactly the costable locus. Thus restricting [A1]'s complex quotient to regular orbits gives exactly that locally-free sheaf locus; the positive-FI stable quotient still contains the non-locally-free boundary. The family and first-order version is conditional on [A2]'s displayed base-change hypotheses and [A3], so no tangent claim is inferred outside that range.

Starting with a framed ASD connection, [A4] constructs its holomorphic Ward bundle; the conditional coupled Penrose and diagonal argument [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]] reconstructs the normalized three-term monad. Starting with regular ADHM data, [A5] identifies its normalized real monad and projection connection with this Ward bundle and connection. The equality of the two constructions is the first-order and inverse-extraction clause in [A5], so it is conditional on that exact real block proof, not on the P² citation alone.

By [A5], both composites on framed isomorphism classes are identities: ADHM data produce the Ward bundle whose monad extraction returns the same $U(k)$ orbit, and an ASD connection produces a Ward bundle whose matrix extraction returns an orbit reconstructing that framed connection. The charge of each resulting connection is $q_N=-k$ by [F2]–[F3]. Thus the claimed bijection and charge statement follow conditionally on [A4]–[A5].

The finite-dimensional quotient and $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf maps are $T$-equivariant by [A1]–[A2]. The Ward construction is natural under rotations and framing transformations by [A4]; the exact matching of its monad torus weights with raw $I,J$ is part of the unresolved convention in [A5]. Once that interface is verified, the composite is $T$-equivariant. The same composition on first-order families is valid only under the base-change hypotheses of [A2]–[A4] and the deformation compatibility of [A5]. This proves the stated conditional torus and tangent clauses and leaves the positive-FI boundary separate.

derivations.claim: When $k=0$, $V=0$. There is exactly one quadruple of maps, all with zero-dimensional domain or codomain. Both moment equations are the unique equality of endomorphisms of $0$; the span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists. Thus this datum is stable and costable, and the quotient by $U(0)$ is one point.

For the framed ASD connection, $q_B=q_N=0$ by [F2], so the ASD action bound gives $F_A=0$. For two piecewise smooth paths from $\infty$ to $x$, their concatenation is a loop and is null-homotopic by [F3]. Pull back a cover by coordinate balls with local parallel frames to the compact homotopy square; a Lebesgue number gives a finite subdivision with each cell mapped into one such ball. Transport along a continuous edge is defined using that ball's parallel frame; on overlaps the change between parallel frames is constant, so the definition is independent of the chosen ball. Each cell has identity boundary transport, and multiplying over the subdivision cancels all interior edges. Therefore the loop holonomy is identity and transport from $\infty$ is path-independent. The resulting sections of a framed orthonormal basis are smooth and parallel in local parallel frames, so the bundle with connection is framed-isomorphic to the trivial bundle with its flat connection. The framing fixes that isomorphism at $\infty$. Any covariantly constant unitary automorphism preserving the framing is identity, since its value at every point is its parallel transport from the identity at $\infty$. Thus the framed flat gauge class is unique and has no residual based stabilizer.

The conditional correspondence of [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]] sends the unique zero-dimensional datum to this unique framed flat ASD class and preserves $q_N=0$. This verifies the $k=0$ boundary without an irreducibility assumption.

derivations.claim: For $V=W=\mathbb C$, both commutators vanish. Thus $\mu_{\mathbb C}=IJ=0$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}=|I|^2-|J|^2=\zeta$. Since $I\ne0$, the words of length zero applied to $I(W)$ span $V$, so the datum is stable. Since $J=0$, the nonzero subspace $V$ is invariant and contained in $\ker J$, so the datum is not costable; in particular it is not a zero-FI regular datum. By [F2], its positive-FI complex orbit has a representative with $I=1$ after the $GL(1,\mathbb C)$ change of basis $g=\zeta^{-1/2}$.

Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.
